properties.program:
# Animation tab: frames 50, play-mode loop
# inputs: amp (swing, radians), len (string length)
view -65, -75, 65, 10

a = amp * sin(2 * pi * t)
x =  len * sin(a)
y = -len * cos(a)

fill "grey"
rect -15, 0, 30, 3
nofill

width 0.5
dash "dash"
line 0, 0, 0, -len - 8
dash "solid"

width 1
line 0, 0, x, y
fill "orange"
circle x, y, 5
nofill

font 4
text 0, -72, "amp %.2f rad   len %.0f", amp, len

properties.text: THE SWINGING PENDULUM -- a Figure node that animates on its own.  Nothing feeds it a time signal: the Figure's Animation tab gives it 50 frames played in a loop at 25 fps, and the program swings the bob with the built-in variable t, which runs from 0 towards 1 over the film.  Spin the wheel over the two knobs while it swings: AMPLITUDE sets how far it swings (radians), LENGTH sets the string.  The swing carries on through every change instead of starting over -- a new value of the same film keeps its frame.  Open the Figure (double-click) to see the program and the Animation tab; the help page explains frame and t.
